symptom: `describe json structure` output of a sample holding `$$` (Teamcenter UID "SR::N::BOMLine..10.7$$Otklm9GclKA") fails `mxcli check` with `token recognition error at: '$$`; the same for a Java/JavaScript action body or EXTRA CODE, an agent prompt or a JSLT step holding `$$`
cause: Every describer wrapped long text as `$$` + text + `$$`, and the lexer's DOLLAR_STRING (`'$$' .*? '$$'`) has no escape, so it ends at the first `$$` in the text; a text ending in `$` breaks it too (the closer pairs with that `$`). The Java/JavaScript `as` and `extra code` positions accepted only DOLLAR_STRING, so there was no other spelling to fall back to
insight:
Route every `$$` emit through one helper that falls back to mdlQuote (the version-aware single-quoted literal: it already handles backslashes and line breaks under mdl 0 and mdl 1) instead of adding PostgreSQL `$tag$` quoting to the lexer: a STRING_LITERAL already spans lines, and every DOLLAR_STRING position but the Java/JS bodies already accepted one. Grep for the delimiter itself, not one spelling of it: the emitters wrote it as "$$", "
as $$
" and "  %s $$
". A round-trip test must parse describe output with its header (describedSource): a headerless parse is mdl 0 and misreads a backslash the mdl 1 fallback writes literally
